style.storyFallback: We're still writing the story of {style} for this page. Until then, the maestros tell it best in the courses below.

son-cubano.p1: **Son** took shape in Oriente, the eastern end of Cuba, in the late 1800s. It joined Spanish song forms and the guitar family with rhythms carried by enslaved Africans and their descendants, above all the Bantu-derived drumming of the region.
son-cubano.p2: By the 1920s it had reached Havana, where groups like the **Sexteto Habanero** and Ignacio Piñeiro's **Septeto Nacional** made it the sound of the city: tres, guitar, bongó, bass, maracas, claves and voices, later a trumpet.
son-cubano.p3: In the 1940s **Arsenio Rodríguez** expanded the band into the conjunto, adding the conga, piano and more trumpets, and stretched the montuno into the long vamp that salsa was later built on.

clave.noteSon: Three strokes in the first bar, two in the second. The bass never plays on one: it anticipates the next chord on the & of 2 and on 4.
clave.noteRumba: Like the son clave, but the third stroke is pushed back to the & of 4.
clave.hear: Hear it on the home page

about.metaDescription: Why Latin Music Mastery exists: authentic Latin music taught by the musicians who play it, with structure and context.
about.title: Keep the music
about.lede: Latin Music Mastery was born from respect for the music, culture and traditions of Latin America.
about.manifestoAccent: Teach the feel, the history and the clave.
about.p1: For generations, Latin music has moved the world with its rhythm and soul, from the syncopated language of Cuban son to the fire of salsa and the sophistication of mambo. These traditions carry stories and musical wisdom that deserve to be preserved and shared.
about.p2: We bring together master musicians, structured lessons and modern practice tools so students anywhere can learn the technique, the history and the cultural foundation behind the music.
about.authenticBody: Every course is taught by a musician who plays that music on stage, in the style's own language.
about.structuredBody: Fundamentals first, then styles, then playing inside the band. Each step builds on the one before.
about.rootedBody: Technique comes with context: where a pattern comes from, who made it famous, and how it sits against the clave.
about.finaleLede: Join the waitlist and be part of the first class of students.

faq.title: Questions,

start.whatA: An online school for Latin music. You learn an instrument from musicians who play it professionally, with HD video lessons, notation synced to every video, and PlaySense feedback while you practice.
start.experienceQ: Do I need any prior musical experience?
start.experienceA: No. Every instrument starts with a fundamentals course that assumes you are new to it. Experienced players can move straight to the style courses.
start.instrumentsA: Courses are live for {list}. More instruments are on the way.
start.instrumentsNone: The first courses are being prepared now. Join the waitlist and we'll tell you as each instrument opens.
start.lessonsA: Each lesson has a video from your maestro with the notation synced underneath. You can slow it down, loop a passage, and play along while PlaySense listens.

billing.costA: Each instrument is {base}/mo, or {annual}/yr. That includes the instrument's fundamentals course plus one style course. Extra style courses are {addon}/mo each.
billing.foundingA: People who join the waitlist before launch keep today's prices when they subscribe.
billing.cancelA: Yes. There are no contracts or cancellation fees. You keep access until the end of your billing period.
billing.secureA: Payments are processed by Stripe. Card details never touch our servers.

playsense.needsA: A microphone on your computer, phone or tablet, or a PlaySense device. Headphones help so the backing track doesn't bleed into the mic.
playsense.downloadQ: Can I download the sheet music?
playsense.downloadA: Yes. Any section can be exported as PDF, MusicXML or MIDI.
